newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian tin, nicket ease on budget duty cuts.
newsitem.headline: Indian tin, nicket ease on budget duty cuts.

text.p: Indian tin and nickel extended losses on Monday on the back of a duty reduction announced in last Friday's budget while copper bounced back on the metal market, dealers said.
Tin and nickel lost 100 rupees each per quintal on fresh selling pressure following cuts in the import duty announced in the budget.
Dealers said tin fell by 100 rupees to 32,200 rupees and nickel fell by the same margin at 37,200 rupees per quintal.
On Saturday tin prices slumped by 2,000 rupees and nickel was down by 400 rupees per quintal.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram has reduced import duty on tin to 20 percent from 30 percent and on nickel to 10 percent from 20.
However he has raised import duty for aluminium to 20 percent from 10 percent. In the open market aluminium was steady at 7,400 rupees per quintal after gaining 75 rupees on Saturday.

Copper rose by 100 rupees to 13,250 rupees per quintal on speculative buying following price hike of 5,000 rupees per tonne announced by the state owned Hindustan Copper Ltd for March. Copper was up by 200 rupees on Saturday.

Zinc was steady at 7,500 rupees per quintal after gaining 100 rupees on Saturday. Sentiment was firm on reports that state-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd has hiked selling prices of zinc by 2,500 rupees per tonne. Lead bounced back by 25 rupees at 4,550 rupees per quintal after falling by 50 rupees on Saturday.
Sentiment was quiet on reports that state-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd. has reduced selling prices of lead by 1,500 rupees per quintal.
